title: SBFRec: Semantic-Behavioral Fusion with Trajectory Smoothing for Generative Sequential Recommendation

problem.claim: Generative sequential recommendation can be brittle when user-history conditional signals are weak, semantic augmentation or routing is unreliable, and generative objectives are misaligned with Top-K ranking under sparse and skewed interactions.

gap.claim: Existing generative approaches do not reliably align conditional signal use and training objectives with Top-K ranking behavior under sparse, skewed interactions.

contributions.claim: SBFRec is a Semantic-Behavioral Flow Matching framework for generative sequential recommendation.
Its stacked dual-branch encoder combines a bidirectional RG-LRU behavioral branch with a sparse MoE semantic adapter and fuses them through a shared residual stream with delta gating.
Popularity-Aware Adaptive Fusion provides sequence-level routing conditioned on popularity profiles to adaptively prefer the more reliable signal source for each sequence.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four benchmark datasets report an average 6.52% improvement over state-of-the-art methods on Top-K ranking metrics.

narrative_sequence.summary: Generative sequential recommendation is vulnerable to weak or unreliable conditional signals and objective mismatch with Top-K ranking, especially under sparse and skewed interactions.
The paper proposes SBFRec, a Semantic-Behavioral Flow Matching framework.
SBFRec combines behavioral and semantic branches through residual-stream fusion with delta gating.
Popularity-aware routing selects branch preferences by sequence profile, while flow-matching decoding and multi-task regularized training encourage complementary signals and prevent branch collapse.
The authors report an average 6.52% improvement over state-of-the-art methods on Top-K metrics across four benchmark datasets.

source_observation.claim: Different sequences may provide more reliable behavioral or semantic signals depending on their popularity profile.

interpretation.claim: Sequence-level adaptive routing may help manage heterogeneous signal reliability.

application.claim: Consider conditioning fusion or routing decisions on observable sequence-level characteristics when input signal quality varies.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether popularity profile is sufficient or generalizes beyond the reported datasets.

source_observation.claim: Dual-branch regularization is used to prevent branch collapse and encourage complementary signals.

interpretation.claim: Explicit regularization can preserve functional diversity among fused branches.

application.claim: When combining heterogeneous representations, include objectives that discourage one branch from dominating without contribution from the others.

exception.claim: The abstract does not specify the regularizer or isolate its effect.

unknowns: The four benchmark datasets are not identified.
The compared state-of-the-art methods are not identified.
The abstract does not report per-dataset results, statistical significance, or ablations.
The abstract does not specify the flow-matching decoder, training objective components, or regularization formulation in detail.
